title.rendered: Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry: Syllabus & Past Papers

content.rendered:
Key Summary

  • One Qualification, Code 4CH1: Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry is a 9 to 1 graded Pearson qualification, examined through two written papers worth 180 marks.
  • Four Content Sections: The syllabus runs across Principles of Chemistry, Inorganic, Physical, and Organic Chemistry, with no coursework and no separate practical paper.
  • Two Routes Now Exist: The established linear route (4CH1) sits alongside a newer modular route, first assessed in June 2025.
  • Resource Heavy Subject: Most searches are for the syllabus, specification, and past papers, so this guide gathers the official Pearson sources in one place.
  • Always Verify With Pearson: Specification issues and grade boundaries change each series, so confirm details against the official Pearson site before you rely on them.

Most students searching for Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry want a few specific things: the real syllabus, the specification, and past papers that match the exam they are sitting. The trouble is that the official specification is a dense PDF, and most sites simply relink it without explaining what any of it means.

This guide does the explaining. It covers what the 4CH1 qualification is, the single and combined science routes, the four syllabus sections, how the two papers differ, how 9 to 1 grading works, a short revision approach, and a clean set of official resources.

Every figure here is checked against the Pearson specification, with honest notes where details change. At Ignite Training Institute, we tutor Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry students across the UAE every term, so this comes from working with the specification and past papers directly.

Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry: The Quick Overview

Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry is the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in Chemistry, specification code 4CH1, graded on the 9 to 1 scale. It is assessed through two externally marked written papers worth 180 marks, covering four sections from principles of chemistry to organic chemistry. There is no coursework, and a calculator is allowed in both papers.

What Is Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry?

Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry is an international qualification from Pearson, usually taken by students aged 14 to 16 before they move on to A-Level. It is built for international centres, including many british curriculum schools across the uae, and is assessed entirely in English.

It was first taught from September 2017, with the first assessment in June 2019, and it carries the same level of demand as the reformed GCSE in England. Other boards offer their own version too, and our overview of IGCSE chemistry across the AQA, CIE and Edexcel boards compares them side by side.

Linear Vs Modular: The Two Routes Explained

For most of its life, Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry has been a linear qualification, which means both papers are sat in the same exam series at the end of the course. Pearson has since added a modular route, first taught from September 2024, first assessed in June 2025, and first certified in August 2025.

The modular route lets units be sat and resat across the June and November series instead of all at the end. Most UAE schools still follow the established linear 4CH1, so check with your school which route you are entered for before you plan your revision.

Know More About: Edexcel IGCSE Physics: Specification, Syllabus, & Resources

Single Chemistry Or Combined Science (Double Award)?

Not every student studying Edexcel chemistry sits the standalone 4CH1 qualification. Pearson offers a few routes, and knowing which one you are on matters for how much content you cover and which paper codes you sit. This decision is part of the broader choice between triple science and combined science that many families encounter. 

Standalone Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry (4CH1) is the full single subject. Students who take Science (Double Award), code 4SD0, study chemistry as one third of a combined science qualification, with reduced content but assessed to the same standard.

There is also a Science (Single Award) option that condenses all three sciences into one GCSE. On the Double Award route, the chemistry Paper 1 shares a code, 4SD0/1C, with the single-subject paper, so the questions look familiar. A student aiming for A-Level Chemistry usually benefits from the depth of the single subject.

Know More About: Edexcel IGCSE Biology: Specification, Syllabus & Study Guide

The Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry Syllabus: Four Core Sections

The 4CH1 specification organises all content into four sections. Every bullet point in the specification can be examined, so a reliable revision plan works through all four rather than betting on favourites.

1. Principles Of Chemistry

This section covers states of matter, atoms and the atomic model, the periodic table, chemical formulae, equations and calculations, ionic and covalent bonding, and electrolysis. This serves as the basis upon which the remainder of the course is constructed, and the concepts of the mole and calculations introduced here are prevalent in both examinations.

2. Inorganic Chemistry

This covers the chemistry of groups in the periodic table, gases in the air, the reactivity series of metals, acids, bases and salts, and the common tests for ions and gases. Practical identification of substances features heavily, and clear knowledge of reactions and observations earns marks.

3. Physical Chemistry

This deals with energetics, rates of reaction, and reversible reactions and equilibria. Students interpret energy changes, reason about collisions and reaction conditions, and work through related calculations. The numerical and graph work here rewards careful, repeated practice.

4. Organic Chemistry

This covers crude oil, alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids, esters, and synthetic polymers. Naming, structures, and reaction types are central, and many of the bold depth statements that appear on Paper 2 sit in this section.

Know More About: How To Study Organic Chemistry Class 12: Smart Exam Tips

How Is Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry Assessed?

The linear 4CH1 qualification is assessed through two written papers, both set and marked by Pearson and both sat in the same series. The table below shows exactly how they differ.

The detail students miss is the depth split. Paper 1 assesses the core content, the statements that are not in bold and carry no ‘C’ reference. Paper 2 assesses everything, including the bold and ‘C’ referenced statements that go further into each topic.

So a student who only revises core content is not ready for Paper 2. The two papers together total 180 marks, and your grade comes from the combined mark, not either paper on its own.

Know More About: Edexcel vs Cambridge: Key Differences You Should Know 2026

How Does 9 To 1 Grading Work In Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry?

Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry is graded on the 9 to 1 scale, where 9 is the highest grade and 1 is the lowest before an unclassified (U) result. It replaced the older A* to G letters, as our breakdown of How IGCSE Grades Work explains in full.

The legacy 4CH0 specification used A* to G, while the current 4CH1 uses 9 to 1. If you are revising now, you are almost certainly on 4CH1, so use 4CH1 materials for the closest match.

How Do Grade Boundaries Work?

A grade boundary is the lowest total mark needed for a given grade in a particular series. These are not fixed. Pearson sets them after each series based on how demanding that session’s papers were, so the mark needed for a 7 can shift from one series to the next.

Boundaries are published as combined raw marks out of 180, not percentages, so always check the official figures for your series rather than relying on last year’s number. The comparisons above are broad guidance, not an official one-to-one equivalence.

Know More About: IGCSE Grades Explained: Grading System, Pass Marks 2026

How To Study For Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry?

Chemistry rewards structured recall and steady past-paper practice more than rereading notes, and timed practice through Ignite’s Test Series helps build exam pace. A few habits tend to move grades on this specification:

  • Work the specification as a checklist. Print the 4CH1 specification and mark each sub-point as secure, shaky, or not yet covered, so nothing slips through.
  • Separate core from depth. Lock down the Paper 1 core content first, then layer on the bold and ‘C’ depth statements that Paper 2 targets.
  • Practise by topic, then by full paper. Topic questions expose weak spots; full timed papers build exam stamina and pace.
  • Learn the equations and tests cold. Mole calculations, formulae, and the ion and gas tests recur every series, so make them automatic.
  • Mark against the official scheme. Chemistry marks go to specific terms, observations, and units, so check answers point by point on the real Pearson mark scheme.

Know More About: How To Study For IGCSE? A Smarter 2026 Method

Where Can You Find Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry Resources?

The resources below are the most practical and trusted sources for Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry. Official Pearson links are kept separate so it is always clear which source is authoritative. Always verify exam information against the official Pearson page.

1. Official Pearson Resources

These are the primary sources for the qualification specification, sample assessments, and grade boundaries. They are the documents to trust over any mirror.

  • Course materials and key documents: The Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry (2017) Course Materials Page
  • Full specification: The Official 4CH1 Specification PDF
  • Sample papers: The Official Sample Assessment Materials
  • Modular route: The Modular Chemistry Specification

2. Official Past Papers And Grade Boundaries

Pearson hosts past papers and grade boundaries directly through its exam materials search. Question papers and mark schemes from the most recent 12 months are restricted to registered exam centres, while older papers are openly available to students. You can browse them on the Pearson past papers search for Chemistry (2017).

When you practise, work the papers that match your route and paper code (4CH1/1C and 4CH1/2C, or the R variants used for some international sittings), and always mark against the matching official scheme.

Know More About: Easiest IGCSE Subjects: Pass Rates, Picks & Cautions 2026

Ignite: Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry Tutors For Confident Exam Preparation

Most students do not lose marks because chemistry is impossible. They lose them because the depth content sneaks up on Paper 2, or because the calculations were never drilled to the point of being automatic. That is the gap structured tutoring closes.

Our Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry Tutoring in Dubai works straight from the 4CH1 specification, separating core from depth and building past-paper practice around the exact papers a student is sitting.

It sits within our wider IGCSE Tutoring Programme, so students get consistent support across their sciences, with revision tied to real mark schemes rather than generic tips.

FAQs

1. Is Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry Hard?

It is demanding but very manageable with steady work. The content is broad rather than tricky, and the main challenge is covering all four sections in enough depth, especially the bold and ‘C’ depth statements that Paper 2 targets. Students who keep up with mole calculations and practise past papers regularly tend to find it fair.

2. How Many Papers Are There In Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry?

Two written papers. Paper 1 (4CH1/1C) runs 2 hours for 110 marks, and Paper 2 (4CH1/2C) runs 1 hour 15 minutes for 70 marks, for a combined total of 180 marks. There is no coursework and no separate practical exam.

3. What Are The Grade Boundaries For Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry?

Grade boundaries are the combined raw marks out of 180 needed for each grade, and Pearson sets them after every series. The difficulty level of the papers changes from year to year, resulting in no set number. It is advisable to always verify the official boundaries for your exam series on the Pearson website.

4. Is A Calculator Allowed In Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry?

Yes. A calculator is allowed in both Paper 1 and Paper 2, and a fair share of marks comes from calculations such as moles, masses, and percentage yield, so practising those quickly is worth the time.

5. Where Can I Find Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry Past Papers?

The most reliable source is Pearson’s own exam materials search. Papers older than 12 months are openly available to students, while the most recent year is restricted to registered centres. Match the paper code and series to your exam, and always mark against the official scheme.

Conclusion

Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry is a clear, well-structured qualification once you can see past the dense specification PDF. The essentials are simple to hold on to: it is 4CH1, graded 9 to 1, two written papers worth 180 marks across four sections, with Paper 2 reaching the harder depth content.

Get the official specification and past papers from Pearson, keep core and depth separate in your revision, and check the grade boundaries for your own series.
